The wake-visual-signals skill now governs the evidence pass: I’ll anchor keyframes to observations, metrics, and diagnostics, compare the strongest run with the most informative contrasting run, and write the diagnosis before editing the policy.

The current rollout set has no failure termination: three independent 0.70-share evaluations are numerically identical successes, while the 0.60-share success is the only informative contrast. The images show the same compact diagonal approach, so I’m treating metric deltas—not visual drama—as the deciding evidence and will use inherited failure records only for safety boundaries.

The evidence points to a conservative one-mechanism candidate: retain the triply reproduced 0.70 posterior share during substantial bearing correction, then taper smoothly toward the faster/lower-effort 0.65 endpoint as the fish aligns. This remains inside evaluated bounds and avoids the failed static gain/guard/damping interpolations. I’m recording that hypothesis now, before changing the executable policy, as required by the wake-visual-signals skill.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated together. The executable change is only the bounded posterior-share schedule; propulsion, steering sign, lag, damping, and both 28-unit guards remain at their reproduced values. I’m moving to schema/syntax checks and the mandated workspace check runner—no CFD rollout.
